frequency_question: How often do authorities that initiate structured secondary market purchase/buyback programs successfully expand them to their target or maximum operational volume within the stated timeline?
membership_rule: Includes formalized central bank or treasury intervention programs with declared operational caps or volume targets; excludes emergency ad-hoc interventions with no scale-up intent.

cases.name: Federal Reserve quantitative easing taper-to-expansion cycles
Bank of Japan JGB purchase program volume adjustments
ECB Pandemic Emergency Purchase Programme (PEPP) volume scaling
Bank of England gilt purchase intervention expansions

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 4 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 4 named historical instances representing primary sovereign debt managers executing structural intervention scale-ups.
known_gaps: Limited to G4 sovereign debt management authorities due to data clarity.
skeleton: 4 major central bank/treasury debt management authorities implementing structural bond intervention programs since 2015, all of which successfully scaled operations to meet or exceed targeted volume thresholds when intended by leadership.
validity_reason: Central bank and treasury operational frameworks for debt management evolve slowly over multi-year institutional horizons.
